claims.text: Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has inadequate oxygen resistance.
Applying an Al2O3 coating to cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr will improve its high-temperature oxygen resistance.
The Al2O3 coating will provide a continuous layer on the alloy surface.
The Al2O3 layer will remain adherent during the specified exposure.
The Al2O3 layer will act as a barrier to oxygen diffusion.
Reduced oxygen diffusion through the coating will lower oxidation of the underlying alloy.
Relative to untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr, coated material will have lower oxidation mass gain after exposure.
Relative to untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr, coated material will have shallower oxide penetration after exposure.
The coating will not significantly alter the alloy's intrinsic mechanical properties.
The room-temperature tensile ductility of coated material will remain comparable to that of untreated material.
The high-temperature yield strength of coated material will remain comparable to that of untreated material.
The proposed applicability boundary is exposure in air at approximately 800 °C for up to 5 hours without applied mechanical load during oxidation.
Performance at much higher temperatures, for longer exposures, or under mechanical loading during oxidation remains untested.
Prolonged or cyclic exposure may produce coating-substrate interactions that affect mechanical properties.
The controlled experiment compares Al2O3-coated and untreated cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr samples after 5 hours in air at 800 °C.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant oxidation reduction, or significant degradation of mechanical properties, is defined as falsifying the hypothesis.
